target: glaucous (PATO_0104277), i.e. a white waxy or powdery bloom; the bearer should also be stem internode (PO_0020142), not stem
fix: In bamboo descriptions, 'white powdery' (also farinose or pruinose) means a waxy or mealy bloom on the surface, not hairs. Map it to glaucous or a bloom value, never to pubescent hair.
reason: The internodes are covered with a white powder when young. That is a waxy bloom, not hair. The words 'young' and 'internodes' are right, but the quality is wrong.

target: veins on the underside of the leaf blade (vascular bundle PO_0005020, abaxial side, part of leaf lamina)
fix: In 'abaxially X on veins', the words 'on veins' narrow the place further. The bearer is the veins on that side, not the whole lower surface.
reason: The flora says only the veins on the lower side are pilose. The annotation makes the whole lower surface pilose.
'Form an interlacing network' means reticulate venation. 'Secondary' is lost, but the primary veins are given separately as parallel, and net secondary venation in Trillium is accurate.

target: purplish green (a mixed hue); green alone drops the purple
fix: A compound colour 'X-Y' (purple-green) means Y tinged with X. It should map to a mixed-colour value or carry both hues, not only the last word.
reason: Mapping the culm sheath to leaf sheath is acceptable. But the colour is purple-green, and 'green' is only part of it.
The flora says the stipules are broad.
The stem is hirsute, strigose or glabrous. All three alternatives are kept.
The leaflets range from linear to oblong. This is a continuum between two shapes.
'Strongly weeping' branches are drooping branches.

target: distal cauline leaf (position slot: distal; whole: stem)
fix: In 'proximal X ...; distal ones N', the count belongs to the distal X only. The position word must be carried into the annotation.
reason: About 4 is the number of distal stem leaves, not of all leaves. Proximal leaves are also present, though withered.
'Bracts and bracteoles ... 1-4 X 0.5-1.5 mm' applies to both, so a bracteole length of 1-4 mm is right.
A basal rosette is sometimes present at anthesis. The stage and the frequency are both kept.
'Herb or shrub' gives two habit alternatives: herbaceous or shrubby.

fix: When a sentence says 'margin entire/undulate/dentate', the bearer is the margin. The quality must not be lifted to the lamina.
reason: The flora explicitly names the margin.
The lower surface of the leaflet blade is part of the leaf's lower surface, so the statement stays true, just less specific. 'Sparsely' only weakens it.
Pinnate venation means the veins are pinnately arranged.

target: whole: male (staminate) flower; part: rudimentary ovary (pistillode)
fix: Statements inside a 'Male flowers ...' block must carry that sex as the whole. 'Rudimentary ovary' means a pistillode, not the ovary itself.
reason: Without the male-flower context, 'ovary absent' is false: the female flowers have ovaries.

target: whole: ray flower (PO_0025331); part: ligule / corolla of the ray floret
fix: In 'Ray-florets ... with white ligules', the colour belongs to the ray-floret corolla. Carry the ray-flower whole.
reason: The disc florets are yellow, so 'petal white' with no ray-floret context is false for this species.
The immature fruit is about 4 mm across. The 'immature' state is kept.
The flora says the sheaths are not septate-nodulose.

target: colour or appearance: greyish-white (hoary), caused by clear leaf hair-points
fix: In mosses, 'hoary' tufts get their grey look from clear awns at the leaf tips. That is a colour/appearance, not a covering of hairs. Do not map it to canescent pilosity.
reason: Grimmia plants do not have hairy surfaces. The hoary look comes from hair-points on the leaves.

fix: In seed descriptions, 'scar' after the testa means the hilum. The shape belongs to the hilum, not the seed.
reason: The seed is obovoid. It is the scar that is roughly elliptic.
The fig receptacle (the fruiting body) is not stalked. Using 'fruit' as the bearer is acceptable for a fig.
The raceme has many flowers. The count word and the inflorescence container are both kept.
Each umbellule (a second-order inflorescence) has 10-14 flowers.
The inner petals are 14-18 mm long, and the 'inner' qualifier is kept.
There are 7 or 8 phyllaries (involucral bracts).
The petals are about 1.5 mm wide.

target: position: base (width at base of the calyx lobe)
fix: A dimension followed by 'at base' or 'at apex' must carry that position. Without it, the reading becomes the overall width.
reason: The flora gives the width at the base of the lobe only.
The ovary is about 10 × 5 mm, so a width of 5 mm is right.

fix: In 'à fleurs glomérulées' ('with clustered flowers'), the clustering belongs to the flowers inside the panicle. Use the flower as the bearer and the inflorescence as the container.
reason: It is the flowers that are clustered, not the inflorescence itself.
